summary: The United States completed its 11th consecutive night of strikes on Iranian military targets across multiple provinces, targeting operations centers, naval capabilities, aircraft hangars, UAV facilities, and logistics infrastructure. Iran launched ballistic missiles from Tabriz and Kermanshah toward Aqaba, Jordan, with explosions heard in Eilat, while Jordan reported intercepting six Iranian missiles. Multiple explosions were reported in eastern Tehran and Pardis, and US strikes hit Behbahan in Khuzestan province.
key_points: CENTCOM confirmed the 11th consecutive night of US strikes on Iran, targeting military operations centers, naval capabilities, aircraft hangars, UAV facilities, and military logistics infrastructure to degrade Iran's ability to threaten commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran launched ballistic missiles from Tabriz and Kermanshah toward Aqaba, Jordan, with explosions heard in Israel's southernmost city of Eilat. (Source: @asafroz/51768, @manniefabian/58824)

Multiple explosions were reported in eastern Tehran and Pardis, Tehran Province, at 2353Z and 03:23 local time. (Source: @shin_persian/8362, @shin_persian/8369)
Iran reports multiple US strikes on regime targets in Behbahan, Khuzestan province. (Source: @New_security8200/202842)

Trump approved the US-Saudi civil nuclear agreement allowing Saudi enrichment of nuclear fuel in civilian reactors on Saudi territory. (Source: @yediotnews25/133043, @yediotnews25/133054)

sections.threat_assessment: The conflict has entered a sustained high-intensity phase with the US conducting 11 consecutive nights of strikes on Iranian military infrastructure across multiple provinces, explicitly targeting Iran's ability to threaten shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran has responded with ballistic missile launches from Tabriz and Kermanshah toward Jordan, demonstrating both reach and willingness to escalate regionally. Trump's explicit threat to strike bridges and power plants in or near Tehran for any Hormuz shipping attack creates a dangerous red line that could trigger rapid escalation. The UK's basing approval for US strikes significantly expands operational capacity. Iran's claimed destruction of a joint US-Israeli-European data center in the UAE suggests prior covert operations. The multi-axis pressure — direct US strikes, Iranian missile retaliation, Gulf state alerts, and Israeli domestic security actions — indicates a broadening conflict with high risk of miscalculation.
sections.regional_response: Jordan actively intercepted Iranian missiles targeting Aqaba, demonstrating operational air defense capability and willingness to engage. Bahrain issued a Seek Shelter alert, indicating credible threat perception. Saudi Arabia secured a landmark civil nuclear agreement with US approval for domestic enrichment, signaling deepened strategic alignment with Washington amid the conflict. Greece advanced a 3 billion euro Israeli air defense procurement (David's Sling, Barak), reflecting regional threat perception extending to NATO members. Lebanon anticipates diplomatic talks with Israel next month at ambassador level, suggesting a potential diplomatic track amid hostilities. The UAE's alleged hosting of a joint intelligence center destroyed by Iran per Iranian claims points to deeper Gulf involvement in targeting Iran.
sections.intelligence_notes: Iran's missile launches from Tabriz (northwest) and Kermanshah (west) indicate dispersed launch infrastructure and ability to threaten multiple vectors. The 11-night sustained US strike campaign suggests a deliberate degradation strategy rather than punitive strikes, targeting command, naval, aviation, UAV, and logistics nodes. CENTCOM's claim of facilitating 900 commercial ships and 450 million barrels through Hormuz since May provides a measurable baseline for shipping security. Iran's claim of destroying a 20-year-old joint data center in the UAE, if verified, represents a significant counter-intelligence achievement. The IDF's public naming of 12 Hamas/PIJ operatives embedded in civilian football structures reveals long-term intelligence penetration of Gaza's military-social fabric. The citizenship revocation request for two Israeli Arabs under a criminal track marks a novel legal tool in counter-terrorism. The UK basing approval, if confirmed, adds a critical logistical enabler for sustained operations.
